name: Dakshina dataset v1.0 (Google Research), Malayalam and Hindi
licence_source: https://github.com/google-research-datasets/dakshina/blob/master/README.md#license ("The dataset is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0"). The repo has no LICENSE file.
attribution: Dakshina dataset by Google Research (Roark et al., 2020, LREC), CC BY-SA 4.0. Native-script text from Wikipedia; romanisations by Google's annotators.
verdict_reason: Share-alike, same position as Wikipedia (see the licence audit). Human romanisations are exactly what the rule probabilities need. Train split for training and for fitting the rule probabilities; dev and test splits held out for eval.
used_for: ml/lexicons/ml.translit.sampled.{train,dev,test}.tsv (native word, romanisation, annotator count), and for M3b the romanized/ rejoined dev and test sentences. Train: transliterator training pairs and the romaniser's rule calibration (training/mlkb/data/calibrate.py). Dev: validation during training. Test: data/eval/translit-human.tsv (2,000 pairs). Dev and test words are kept out of every training pair. The native_script_wikipedia text (a copy of mlwiki) isn't used. M3b: romanized/ rejoined dev sentences: data/eval/next-manglish*.tsv (eval only). Test sentences untouched. Both splits' sentences are removed from the M3b LM training text. The romaniser calibrated on the train split also writes the M3b synthetic Manglish LM text. Hindi pack (hi/): hi/lexicons/hi.translit.sampled.{train,dev,test}.tsv the same way (train: Hindi transliterator pairs and the check of the Hindi romanisation table, data/lang/hi/romanisation.json; dev: validation; test: data/eval/hi/translit-human.tsv). Dev and test words are kept out of every Hindi training pair. hi/romanized/ rejoined dev sentences: Hinglish eval only (data/eval/hi/next-hinglish*.tsv); test sentences untouched. Both splits' sentences are removed from the Hindi LM's training text (by hash, in both scripts), whose Hinglish is synthetic, from Hindi's spelling table. Tamil (ta/), eval only: ta/romanized/ rejoined dev sentences are the Tanglish next-word sets data/eval/ta/next-tanglish*.tsv (training/mlkb/eval/next_sets.py --lang ta); test sentences untouched. The Tamil pack trains on nothing of Dakshina's: its transliterator's human pairs are Aksharantar's, its LM text is the pack's own sources, and the eval sentences are removed from that text by hash, in both scripts. Kannada (kn/), eval only: kn/lexicons/kn.translit.sampled.test.tsv (5,047 pairs of 2,500 words) is typed into packs/kn.neopack with training/mlkb/eval/pack.py --set, a second held-out measurement beside Aksharantar's manual test rows; the set is built in a scratch folder and not committed. The Kannada pack trains on nothing of Dakshina's: Aksharantar's Dakshina rows are dropped by the filter, its transliterator's pairs are Aksharantar's mined rows and its own words spelled by its tables, and it has no LM. Most of these words (2,414 of 2,500) are also targets of Aksharantar's mined training rows, which the numbers report separately. Punjabi (pa/), eval only: pa/lexicons/pa.translit.sampled.test.tsv (6,988 pairs of 2,500 words) is typed into packs/pa.neopack with training/mlkb/eval/pack.py --set, a second held-out measurement beside Aksharantar's manual test rows; the set is built in a scratch folder and not committed. The Punjabi pack trains on nothing of Dakshina's: Aksharantar's Dakshina rows are dropped by the filter, its transliterator's pairs are Aksharantar's mined rows and its own words spelled by its tables, and it has no LM. Most of these words (2,396 of 2,500) are also targets of those training pairs, which the numbers report separately. Dakshina has no Odia.
retrieved: 2026-11-03 (ml); 2026-11-06 (hi); 2026-11-11 (ta, from the same tar); 2026-11-12 (kn and pa, from the same tar)
notes: The tar holds all 12 languages (2,008,340,480 bytes). After data/fetch.sh, extract only the Malayalam lexicons: tar -xf data/raw/dakshina/dakshina_dataset_v1.0.tar -C data/raw/dakshina 'dakshina_dataset_v1.0/ml/lexicons/*'. The SHA-256 of each extracted file is under `extracted`. For M3b: tar -xf data/raw/dakshina/dakshina_dataset_v1.0.tar -C data/raw/dakshina 'dakshina_dataset_v1.0/ml/romanized/*' (training/mlkb/lm/sources.py does this). Hindi: tar -xf data/raw/dakshina/dakshina_dataset_v1.0.tar -C data/raw/dakshina dakshina_dataset_v1.0/hi/lexicons dakshina_dataset_v1.0/hi/romanized.
